_comment: The config gitsieve uses on itself, in CI and via `npm run selfcheck`.
It carries no `terms`: a real terms list names the strings you are trying
not to publish and belongs outside the repository. What is safe to commit
is this -- suppressions that reference findings by id, and a control string
that is public by definition because it is already in the repository.

controls.note: present in package.json and the README; zero matches here means the scanner is not reading file contents

suppress.reason: AWS publishes this key id in its own documentation as a non-functional example. It is planted in a test fixture so the secret check has something real to find. The literal is deliberately not repeated here: a suppression file that quotes the value it suppresses becomes the finding.
